habit_scope: Sequence step after trusses or rafters: wood structural panel roof deck. HUD §5.6.4: typically 8d, min 6 in o.c. edges / 12 in o.c. field, also 6 in at gable-end; commonly 7/16–5/8 in. CMHC Fig 97 6/12 min is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not copy wall WSP 6/12 onto the roof as if it were this HUD paragraph. Hurricane 8d ring-shank 6 in all / 4 in gable is not Wasatch/Fontana habit.
how_it_is_done: Trusses plumbed and temp-braced, or rafters/joists in. CMHC: stiffness of the roof increases when sheathing is applied. HUD: properly attached roof sheathing provides adequate overall bracing of the truss system except long compression webs.

Panels: plywood or OSB. AF&PA: long dimension perpendicular to rafters; continuous over two or more spans; recommended spans, edge spacing, and thickness STAMPED ON THE PANEL. FM: plywood sheathing similar to wall sheathing except laid perpendicular to rafters and trusses. CMHC Fig 97: face grain at right angles to framing; joints offset.

Gap: CMHC leave 2 to 3 mm (1/8 in) between panels to prevent buckling. AF&PA roof text does not reprint the 1/8 in; floor subfloor 1/8 in is not this roof number — use CMHC 1/8 in as Canadian and the panel stamp / AHJ for US.
Unsupported edges: CMHC metal H-clip, blocking, or T&G. Thin panels: 2x2 blocking or H-clips.

Nailing: HUD §5.6.4 — generally nails min 6 in o.c. at edges and 12 in o.c. at intermediate supports; also 6 in at gable-end framing; nail size typically 8d (thinner power-driven nails most commonly used). Roof sheathing commonly 7/16- to 5/8-in. CMHC Fig 97 — 150 mm (6 in) o.c. minimum edges / 300 mm (12 in) o.c. minimum field. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Keep both. Do not copy wall BWL 6/12 as if it were this paragraph. Hurricane: 8d ring-shank 6 in all / 4 in gable is high-wind CLASS, not Wasatch/Fontana habit.

Lumber sheathing (CMHC): closed, ends supported, joints staggered; boards 8 in nominal or less: at least two 51 mm (2 in) nails per bearing; wider: at least three. High wind: 63 mm (2-1/2 in) nails. Boards >12 in nominal should not be used. High wind/earthquake: lumber sheathing diagonal or engineered.

Spaced sheathing: AF&PA / CMHC for wood shingles/shakes only. AF&PA: 18-in felt between shake courses; wind-driven snow → solid sheathing + Type 15 felt under shakes. Not the asphalt-shingle habit deck.

Valleys/hips: CMHC fit sheathing tight and nail to the valley/hip rafter. Chimney: 50 mm (2 in) clearance wood to masonry (Fig 99); may reduce to 12 mm (1/2 in) for exterior masonry chimneys — Canadian / confirm AHJ.

Cover without delay. CMHC: roof covering as soon as the sheathing is in place to keep the building dry. AF&PA: buildings should be roofed and enclosed with sheathing without delay. Next method is m-P09-roof-felt (FM roofing felt underlay).
tools_equipment: Named: metal H-clips (CMHC). Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Long dimension / face grain perpendicular to framing (AF&PA; CMHC Fig 97; FM).
Continuous over two or more spans (AF&PA).
1/8 in gap (CMHC 2-3 mm) — Canadian / confirm AHJ.
H-clip, blocking, or T&G at unsupported edges (CMHC).
HUD §5.6.4 typically 8d, 6 in edges / 12 in field, also 6 in at gable-end. CMHC Fig 97 6/12 min is Canadian. Keep both.
2 in chimney clearance unless AHJ reduces (CMHC / AF&PA).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the dry-in deck step on truss or stick. Spaced sheathing is only for wood shingles/shakes (AF&PA / CMHC), not the asphalt habit.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Copying wall 6/12 as if it were an IRC roof nail table. Using CMHC 6/12 as a US stamp. Skipping H-clips on thin panels. Walking a Utah ice pack onto a Fontana deck.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They sheathe. What they skip is the 1/8 in gap, H-clips, and that the US penny is the panel stamp, not a copied wall schedule.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Panel span rating / thickness on drawings. Confirm with AHJ / engineer / panel stamp. Do not invent IRC R803.2.
risk_if_swapped_late: Changing 24 in truss module after the deck is on means ripping sheathing. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: After the trusses or rafters are in, the deck is plywood or OSB, long way across the framing, with a small gap so it does not buckle. Unsupported edges get H-clips or blocking. HUD says nails are typically 8d, 6 on the edges and 12 in the field, and 6 at the gable end. The Canadian book prints 6 and 12 as a minimum — that is NBC, confirm the AHJ. Do not copy the wall bracing 6/12 and call it this paragraph. Cover the house as soon as the deck is on.
spanish_summary: Con las cerchas o tijeras ya puestas, el forro es plywood u OSB a lo largo atravesando el armazon, con junta chica. Bordes sin apoyo: H-clip o blocking. HUD: clavos por lo general 8d, 6 en el borde y 12 en el campo, y 6 en el gable. El libro canadiense pone 6 y 12 como minimo — es NBC. No copie el 6/12 de las paredes y lo llame este parrafo. Cubra en cuanto este el forro.
locators: CMHC Ch12 Fig 97 printed 136 / txt 7763-7818: 6 in edge min / 12 in field min; 1/8 in gap; H-clip. Canadian / confirm AHJ.
AF&PA Roof Sheathing txt 817-833: 4x8 panels; stamp on face; long way perpendicular; two or more spans; spaced sheathing + Type 15 under shakes.
FM 5-426 Roof Decking txt 3729-3733: plywood perpendicular to rafters and trusses.
AF&PA txt 274-277: roofed and enclosed with sheathing without delay. CMHC txt 7969-7971: covering as soon as sheathing is in place.
HUD RSDG §5.6.4 (txt 12647-12677): typically 8d, 6 in edges / 12 in field, also 6 in at gable-end; commonly 7/16–5/8 in. Hurricane ring-shank CLASS not habit.
confidence_notes: Panel orientation and delay-to-cover high. HUD §5.6.4 typically 8d 6/12 + gable-end 6 in is the US schedule. CMHC 6/12 min kept as Canadian. Hurricane ring-shank is not habit.
remodel_note: Reroofing is FM technique, not this new-house deck method.

fastener_schedule.size: typically 8d (sinker, box, or common; IRC requires common but also permits staples; power-driven used extensively)
fastener_schedule.pattern: to roof rafters/trusses; also 6 in at gable-end framing
fastener_schedule.oc: min 6 in o.c. edges / 12 in o.c. field; 6 in at gable-end
fastener_schedule.source: HUD RSDG §5.6.4 (txt 12656-12665). Typically 7/16–5/8 in panels. Hurricane 8d ring-shank 6 in all / 4 in gable is NOT Wasatch/Fontana habit.

fastener_schedule.what: WSP roof sheathing to framing (CMHC Canadian)
fastener_schedule.size: not printed as a US penny
fastener_schedule.pattern: face grain / long dimension perpendicular; joints offset
fastener_schedule.oc: 150 mm (6 in) o.c. minimum edges; 300 mm (12 in) o.c. minimum field
fastener_schedule.source: CMHC Fig 97 printed 136. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. US size+oc: panel stamp / AHJ (gap-P09-us-roof-sheathing-nail-size).

fastener_schedule.what: lumber roof boards 8 in nominal or less (CMHC)
fastener_schedule.size: 51 mm (2 in) nails; 63 mm (2-1/2 in) in high wind
fastener_schedule.pattern: at least two per bearing; ends supported; joints staggered
fastener_schedule.source: CMHC Ch12 txt 7809-7815. Canadian / confirm AHJ.

fastener_schedule.what: lumber roof boards wider than 8 in nominal (CMHC)
fastener_schedule.size: 51 mm (2 in) nails; 63 mm (2-1/2 in) in high wind
fastener_schedule.pattern: at least three per bearing. Boards >12 in nominal should not be used.

1/8 in gap (CMHC 2-3 mm) — Canadian / confirm AHJ.
H-clip, blocking, or T&G at unsupported edges (CMHC).

Panel face stamp (AF&PA). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
